pr_title: Implement target discovery in own k8s namespace
pr_body:
This commit adds support for discovering targets from the same
Kubernetes namespace as the Prometheus pod itself. Own-namespace
discovery can be indicated by using `"."` as the namespace.

Fixes #9782

Signed-off-by: fpetkovski <filip.petkovsky@gmail.com>

pr_comments:
Apologies for not commenting on the original issue. I don't think I'm a fan of the magic value, though I agree that it probably shouldn't be mutually exclusive to the name-list. How about we still have the explicit field of `includeOwnNamespace` or something like that, and essentially concatenate that with the list specified in `names`.

cc @roidelapluie

Okay, we can have `own_namespace: bool`: Add current namespace to the namespaces to watch. If `namespaces` is not set, only the current namespace will be monitored.

I would not call it "include" because the default namespaces include it already (because it does not filter on namespace)
Thanks both for the feedback. I updated the PR with an explicit `own_namespace` variable instead of relying on a magic value. PTAL again :)

issue_context.title: Support target discovery in the same kubernetes namespace with prometheus pod without explicit namespace config
issue_context.body:
<!--

    There is also commercial support available.

    https://prometheus.io/support-training/

-->
## Proposal
Support target discovery in the same kubernetes namespace with prometheus pod without explicit namespace config
With this feature, we can use the same prometheus config when deploying prometheus in different kubernetes namespace.
The namespace can be got from `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/namespace` file.
An config item need to be added, and the config file may be like following.
```
    scrape_configs:
     - job_name: 'kubernetes-pods'
       kubernetes_sd_configs:
        - role: pod
          in_cluster_namespace: true
```
comments:
I think this generally makes sense. We do already have the `namespaces` configuration field, which has a nested object so we could do something like:

```
namespaces:
  own: true
```

And make it mutually exclusive with the `names` sibling.

Since namespaces is a list of strings, could we use an invalid namespace ID as "magic" value? e.g. 

```
namespaces: ["."]
```
(I would not make it exclusive)

Precedent: in alertmanager, we also have a special dottet notation that uses dots for labels: `group_by: [...]`

review_comments: This test makes sure that all namespace discovery is not broken by the new feature
